classification.difficultyReason: Calculate one gradient from coordinates, then use parallel and perpendicular sides of a rectangle to infer two further gradients.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangle on coordinate axes, without ticks or grid. A(2,4) is below-left of B(3,6); C is above the horizontal axis and D below it. AD crosses the horizontal axis. Decorative blue edges and red dots are rendered black in house style.
spec.mathematics: ABCD is a rectangle; only A(2,4) and B(3,6) are numerical givens. Unlabelled coordinates used to construct C and D are schematic rendering coordinates, not additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied diagram remains visible in every edition. No calculated gradients are shown in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
Opposite sides of a rectangle are parallel, so $CD\parallel AB$ and their gradients are equal.

$$m_{CD}=m_{AB}=2.$$

Adjacent sides of a rectangle are perpendicular, so their gradients have product $-1$.

$$\begin{align*}2m_{AD}&=-1\\m_{AD}&=-\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$
